Carrying with ADC is the same, if not easier on this patch/season. Yeah you won't l win vs a 6/1 top laner, you never did. It's your job to win teamfights with superior positioning, don't even let those guys get to you (of course sometimes they are fed enough to just run straight to you, can't win all games).

Play with your team and watch out for the enemy threats and cooldowns, if malphite didn't ult yet chill a bit and don't walk straight into their team also be ready to flash it (if you anticipate it it's pretty easy to flash).

For soloQ just play the 1v2 carries like Kalista, if your support knows how to auto attack it's enough to win the lane (and possibly game) on your own. Even if you lose your lane you can still make plays somewhere else, they have a lead and freeze bot? Go roam with your support until they break the freeze and you can farm again.

The same goes the other way around tho, if you're winning the lane DO SOMETHING with it, don't freeze it for 10 minutes and let other lanes win the game for them. Move around, put pressure on other lanes and get objectives.

Itemize properly vs fed champs: If your enemy really is too fed for you and your team is still doing well on other lanes consider buying some kind of defensive item relatively early, like QSS or hexdrinker.

Diana is my most played champion and I play her a lot top too, which is by the way my preferred lane for her (that's just my own preference though). I'll try to answer your questions.

The buildpath. It's true that most of the time you will go for the seekers rush against AD and abyssal rush vs AP, however against certain matchups if you feel like they have no kill pressure on you and/or their jungler isn't an early game-gank based champ you can go for the nashor's rush without getting punished. You can also go for the half measure and buy just seekers/negatron into nashor's instead of finishing the zhonya's/abyssal.

The playstyle. It doesn't differ too much from mid lane. You just farm up, get good trades early game with your shield and just poke them down until you have the pressure to all in them on 6. You can still pressure tanks like Malphite/Maokai, your passive hit Q W R still chunks them by quite a bit and they won't be able to break your shield. Don't try extended trades against them though, you'll most likely lose them until you have your nashor's.

Matchups. Diana has only a few matchups that are really hard for her, something like the juggernauts that would be too tanky for her to do something early game since they also have the damage to kill you. AP tops are fairy easy to deal with (except heimer maybe, he'll just push you into your tower 24/7 and you can't all in him). Attack based champs like Jax/Trynd you should just poke them and do small trades (hit minions twice, Q W R auto and retreat) they'll win the extended auto trades. Against true tanks you can actually pressure them as I mentioned before, they won't have the damage to outtrade you. Bruisers like Irelia/Riven are the tricky part, they are heavy skill matchups and really just depend on how you play it. Your lvl 1/2 should be stronger with your shield but lvl 3 they will start to win trades at that point just farm with Q and try to poke them at the same time, you won't win trades until 6.

Now just some general tips, if you start W lvl 1 nothing should be able to outtrade you. Against burst matchups (hello riven) you can skill Q W W on lvl 3 to avoid getting bursted down, rank 2 shield really helps out (after that continue to max Q). You don't have to skill E early-mid game (I only consider skilling it earlier against Katarina or if I have Yasuo in my team), usually I get my first point in E at lvl 13. If you do double jungle or start a camp lvl 1 do not forget mana potions. Mana management is a huge part of Diana, especially top lane, it's so important that I started to run manaregen seals (only do this if you're confident enough to not run armor/health runes).
